ScoreDeprecation.description: RFC 9745 deprecation date of the 0–100 score (2026-09-02T00:00:00Z).

Vet402Signature.description: Ed25519 signature over RFC 8785 (JCS) bytes of `{"v":1,"path":<pathname+search>,"signedAt":<UTC seconds>,"body":<JSON>}`. Omitted when VET402_RESPONSE_SIGNING_KEY is unset. See docs/response-signatures.md.

AgentId.description: ERC-8004 agent token ID (uint256 as decimal string)
AgentId.name: agentId

VerifyWallet.description: Optional wallet to verify against agent's registered wallet
VerifyWallet.name: wallet

RateLimited.description:
Rate limit exceeded. On authenticated paths this means the monthly quota
is spent (`rate_limit_exceeded`); on key-less paths it is the per-IP
window (`rate_limited`).

RateLimit-Limit.description: Key-less paths — ceiling for the IP window. Sent on every response.

RateLimit-Remaining.description: Key-less paths — requests left in your current IP window. Per-caller, so it is sent here and on other uncached responses, but not on a CDN-cached 200.

RateLimit-Reset.description: Key-less paths — unix epoch seconds when your window resets. Same per-caller rule as RateLimit-Remaining.

X-RateLimit-Remaining.description: Authenticated paths — quota left this month.

X-RateLimit-Used.description: Authenticated paths — quota consumed this month.

AccuracyInterpretation.description: The caveats that qualify every rate in this document, in the same words the human page at /accuracy prints beside them. Present so a machine reader never has to parse the HTML to learn what a figure means.

caveats.description: Human-readable sentences, generated from the counts in this same response rather than hard-coded, so they cannot go stale when the sample changes.

detectionRateCountsWarnAsDetection.description: True: operatorBenchmark.knownBad.detectionRate counts a WARN as a detection, so a caller that lets WARN through is not protected by it.

externalFiguresExcludeOperatorBenchmark.description: True — the self-seeded benchmark is partitioned out at the query layer.

falsePositiveRateCountsBlockOnly.description: True: operatorBenchmark.knownGood.falsePositiveRate counts only a BLOCK on a known-good address, so 0% means "none were blocked", not "all were passed".

knownBadWarnOnly.description: How many known-bad addresses stopped at WARN rather than BLOCK.

minSample.description: Below this many resolved verdicts a rate is null rather than a number.

allowAdverseRate.description: Of ALLOW verdicts with a known outcome, the share that went bad.

blockFalsePositiveRate.description: Of BLOCK verdicts with a known outcome, the share later confirmed legitimate.

coverageWeekly.description: How much of the listed catalog was measured in the last 7 days (null when unreachable).

generatedAt.description: Quote this when citing a figure — the rates move as the sample grows.

l0.description: L0 false-fail / false-pass over the last 7 days (null when the store is unreachable).

observedVerdicts.description: Distinct verdicts with any outcome recorded, including neutral-only.

operatorBenchmark.description: Self-seeded controlled test against a fixed, versioned address set. Excluded from every field above at the SQL layer.

lastBroadScan.description: Latest UTC day whose scans covered at least half of the addresses in the window. Since 2026-11-02.

lastScanAddresses.description: Addresses scanned on the UTC day of lastScanAt. Since 2026-11-02.

resolvedVerdicts.description: Distinct verdicts whose outcome resolves to good or bad.

slo.description: Freshness / reverse-lookup / evidence-completeness SLOs with their targets (null when unreachable).

facts_summary.description: L0-L2 measurement records for endpoints paid to the agent's wallet, the first 3 of total_endpoints.

proof.description: Everything a third party needs to re-verify control without trusting this server: run verifyMessage(message, signature, wallet), then confirm wallet == getAgentWallet(agentId) on-chain.

score.description: Best-effort. null when the agent could not be scored; the passport is still valid.

verified.description: Whether a signed identity claim exists for this agent.

paidAttempts30d.description: Same as sellers.json paid_attempts_30d for the matched endpoint row.

BenchmarkSide.description: Counts for one half of the operator benchmark. Each labelled address is counted once, using its most recent scan.

allowed.description: known-good only — ALLOW, i.e. true negatives.

detected.description: known-bad only — BLOCK or WARN. See interpretation.detectionRateCountsWarnAsDetection.

falsePositiveRate.description: known-good only — BLOCK on a known-good address. null below minSample.

missed.description: known-bad only — ALLOW, i.e. false negatives.

BuyerFacts.description: §8.2 buyer facts for a Payer / Agent (role=payee decisions).

retry_burst_rate.description: Former name of short_interval_payment_rate, with the same value. Settled rows do not show whether a payment was a retry.

short_interval_payment_rate.description: Share of the gaps between this payer's settled payments to the same resource that are 60 s or shorter, over each raw settlement row of the 30-day window. It describes payment timing and does not change the recommendation. null with no data.

unavailable.description: Sybil signals that could not be read, by name.

CallerPolicy.description: The caller's policy, applied by the server to the decision it sits beside (WINDOW_PLAN §16.3, 2026-09-07). Same order as the SDK's payOrRefuse: ceiling first, then degraded, then BLOCK, then not-ALLOW (unless waived with `require_vet402_allow=false`), then the L1 floor. `verdict` REFUSE carries the first gate that failed, in the SDK's own word; ALLOW carries none. It never rewrites `recommendation` — a waived WARN stays a WARN next to a caller_policy ALLOW, and the reader combines the two. BLOCK and degraded are never lifted by a floor or a waiver.

applied.description: What was applied. `amount_usd` is null when the caller did not name it (then the ceiling is not evaluated).

not_evaluated.description: What the server did not check. `min_subgraph_receipts` is always listed — The Graph's subgraph is read only with the caller's own Gateway key, by the SDK / pay_if_trusted. `max_per_tx_usd` is listed when `amount_usd` was not sent.

reason_codes.description: SDK vocabulary (packages/sdk PayRefuseReason), unchanged. Empty on ALLOW.

CensusSummary.description: §7.2 / §9.1 settlement census. `settlements_raw` and `settlements_real` are always both present and never merged.

indexed_since.description: How far back the index actually reaches. `window` is the period asked for, not the period held. Measured 2026-09-04 in production, eip155:8453 started 2026-08-23 (13 of the 30 requested days) while solana started 2026-07-21 (46 days), so a single overall date would hide that the chain carrying 99.9% of the rows covers 13 days. When `window_fully_covered` is false the counts in this response are a floor, not a total.

all.description: Oldest UTC day (YYYY-MM-DD) the index holds for any chain; null when nothing is indexed.

all_chains_since.description: Oldest UTC day from which every listed chain is indexed (the latest of the byChain days).

byChain.description: Oldest indexed UTC day per CAIP-2 chain. One entry when `chain` is set.

note.description: What is counted and what is not

window_covered_days.description: Whole UTC days of the requested window, ending today, that the index holds for each listed chain (from all_chains_since).

window_fully_covered.description: False when any listed chain's index does not reach back a full window.

measurement.description: Payers on the published measurement list (wash_flag measurement).

CheckSellerDocument.description: Structured content of MCP `check_x402_seller` and key-less GET `/api/v1/check`. Matches src/lib/mcp/schemas.ts `checkSellerOutput`.

next_action.description: Plain-language next step after ALLOW, WARN, or BLOCK (verdictNextStep).

verified_pay_to_by_network.description: Since 2026-11-22. Recipients vet402 paid and confirmed delivery to, per chain. If the network and payTo pair of the 402 you received is not here, vet402 has not verified the recipient on that network. Empty when the URL is not in the catalog.

CorrectionRow.description: §10. One published verdict that changed after publication. Rows are never deleted.

after.description: The published value after the correction.

before.description: The published value before the correction.

settlement_path.description: For settlement_backfill rows, the path the row took, derived from before/after when read; null for other reasons. Since 2026-09-29.

nextCursor.description: Pass back as ?cursor= for the next older page; null on the last page.

total.description: Rows matching endpoint and reason, regardless of cursor. Since 2026-09-29.

CoverageWeekly.description: §12 weekly coverage — how much of the listed catalog was actually measured.

DataDepth.description:
How much receiving history this score could draw on. `thin` wallets lean more
heavily on wallet-health and outflow-pattern signals since there isn't much
settlement track record yet; `rich` wallets are judged mostly on that track
record. Integrators should treat a `thin` score as lower-confidence.

DecisionReasonCode.description: Since 2026-11-13.1. The reason codes of `DecisionResult.reason_codes`: the fixed words in `enum`, plus the families in `x-vet402-patterns` (l0_unverified_<cause>, <input>_unavailable). Meaning, effect on the verdict, what it means for the payer and whether the seller can fix it: /docs/api#reason-codes (same source, src/lib/decision/reason-codes.ts).

DecisionResult.description: Product spec §9.1. A pre-payment (role=payer) or pre-service (role=payee) decision. `facts` and `recommendation` always travel in the same document; there is no facts-less mode. `score` is the transitional 0–100 opinion, present only with `include_score=1` (since 2026-09-29.3), and is never the basis of `recommendation`.

caller_policy.description: Present only when `amount_usd`, `max_per_tx_usd`, `min_l1_deliveries` or `require_vet402_allow` was sent (2026-09-07). The caller's own rule applied server-side, in the SDK's words. Absent otherwise — the no-policy body is unchanged.

degraded.description: True when an input could not be measured; the recommendation is then fail-closed.

evidence.description: Public receipts behind the facts. Every row names its own `source`; `/decision` emits only `vet402` rows.

evidence_age.description: Since 2026-11-15, last delivery age from a paid test for role payer, first in the JSON object, null for role payee.

facts.description: L0–L2 measurement records — SellerFacts for role=payer, BuyerFacts for role=payee. Never contains a trustScore.

freshness.description: Observation times of l0 / l1 / l2 (ISO 8601 or null).

l1_basis.description: What the L1 part of the recommendation read (rules 2026-09-29.2). Null for role=payee. Counts are over the 30-day window; times are ISO 8601 UTC. ALLOW needs a delivery within fresh_days.

fresh_days.description: ALLOW needs the last delivery within this many days (30, the re-buy interval for a seller that has already delivered).

last_attempt_at.description: Same as facts.l1.last_attempt_at (any outcome, full history).

last_delivered_at.description: Last delivery over the full history.

last_signed_attempt_at.description: Last signed paid attempt over the full history.

latest_counted_delivered.description: Whether the latest counted attempt delivered; null when none is counted.

n_counted.description: Signed attempts counted for or against the seller: those that delivered or that /sellers puts on the seller's side.

n_not_counted.description: n_attempts − n_counted: attempts on vet402's side, held, not yet known to have moved money, taking no payment, or not sorted to a side on /sellers. Includes facts.l1.n_inconclusive (the held subset the purchases route reports). l1_inconclusive is the case n_not_counted = n_attempts > 0.

n_paid_undelivered.description: Signed attempts that moved money (settled on-chain, or a settle_failed row whose transaction vet402 verified) and did not deliver, leaving out vet402's side and held attempts.

n_paid_undelivered_seller_side_since_las.description: Of those, the ones /sellers puts on the seller's side (seen on two different UTC days). 2 or more is a BLOCK. Since 2026-09-29.4.

n_paid_undelivered_since_last_delivery.description: Of those, the ones after the last delivery in the window (all of them when nothing was delivered). 1 or more is at least a WARN.

not_attempted_reason.description: Sub-code for `l1_not_attempted`, present when that reason code is in `reason_codes` and the record names one of these two causes. `spending_halted`: vet402 stopped its own spending — a fact about the measurer. `no_eligible_accept`: the wall offered nothing machine-payable, so nothing was signed. Null otherwise, including the other ways an attempt can end before the signature (over cap, price mismatch, payee mismatch): those are published per attempt in the decision ledger at `/api/v1/observatory/decisions`, not summarised here.

payer.description: payer_id (chain:address) when role=payee; null for role=payer.

reason_codes.description: Machine-readable reasons. Every code, with its meaning, what it means for the payer and whether the seller can fix it, is in `DecisionReasonCode` and in the table at /docs/api#reason-codes. Rules 2026-11-13.1 (rules_version). Each paid attempt (one L1 purchase row) is sorted by one function, the same one /sellers, /api/v1/sellers/export.csv and this decision read: whether money moved, whether it delivered, and whose side a failure is on. Money moved when the payment settled on-chain, or when a settle_failed row carries a transaction vet402 verified; it did not move when vet402 signed nothing or the transaction the seller named was not found; otherwise it is not yet known. The outcome is one of: delivered (settled on-chain, then a 2xx other than 202 Accepted, with a non-empty body); pending (not yet known whether money moved: a receipt awaiting on-chain verification, a 2xx naming a transaction, or a signed attempt that failed less than 90 minutes ago while vet402 links late settlements; the ledger status is left as recorded); seller (the seller's side: vet402 can show from the row that the failure was not its own, and such a failure, of any kind, was seen at the listing on 2 or more different UTC days); vet402 (vet402's side: its wallet was short, it did not send the declared input, or one of its own limits or errors); unsorted (not sorted: held for vet402's own request shape, no charge taken, a paid answer with no result in it, seen on one UTC day so far, or vet402 cannot show the failure was not its own); not_bought (vet402 did not sign a payment, so it is not a purchase result). An attempt counts for or against the seller only when it delivered or is on the seller's side; every other signed attempt is left out with an l1_not_counted_* code (l1_not_counted_held counts held rows except seller_fixable_input, plus a receipt awaiting on-chain verification whose held_reason is empty). A settled 400 or 422 whose paid request carried every declared input and whose bodyHead parses as JSON with a structured input validation error (FastAPI/pydantic detail[].loc, zod issues[].path, or errors[].field|path|param with in or location on body or query, not free text, with every cited location on the request input, not payment, headers, cookies or authentication) is counted on the seller's side once seen on 2 different UTC days. In the decision it counts as a seller-side attempt (l1_latest_failed or l1_never_delivered, WARN) but never as l1_paid_not_delivered and never toward a BLOCK. /api/v1/sellers/export.csv follows /sellers. The ledger export.csv does not change. L1: after the last delivery in the 30-day window, an attempt that moved money and did not deliver adds l1_paid_not_delivered; it is a BLOCK only when two or more of them are on the seller's side (seen on 2 different UTC days), and a WARN otherwise, including when /sellers leaves them not sorted. A failure where no money moved is at most a WARN (l1_never_delivered when nothing was ever delivered). When no result came back and it is not yet known whether money moved (an empty 2xx with no settlement linked, a receipt still awaiting on-chain verification, or a signed attempt that failed less than 90 minutes ago), l1_empty_2xx_settlement_unknown makes it a WARN, never an ALLOW, until it settles. l1_latest_failed (something delivered, but the latest counted attempt did not) is a WARN. ALLOW needs a delivery within 30 days (l1_basis.fresh_days); otherwise l1_stale and a WARN, also the word when the only delivery is older than the window or every signed attempt is (l1_not_attempted means none was ever signed). l1_basis carries the counts, the last attempt, signed attempt and delivery, and the days since each. L0: l0_fail (two measured failures in a row) is a BLOCK. l0_unverified (not probed yet, no probe in the last 30 days, a URL with a path parameter vet402 cannot fill, a probe that could not complete, or one failure so far) is a WARN with degraded: true, next to l0_unverified_<cause>; unverified is not a failure. L2: l2_mismatch is a BLOCK when the evidence names missing keys (mismatch_kind missing_keys), otherwise l2_mismatch_unexplained and a WARN. L2 reads the latest delivery at any age, so a mismatch holds until a later delivery replaces it. A listing that declares an output schema but whose latest delivery vet402 has not checked against it (no delivery, a body over 256 KiB or cut off) is l2_not_checked, a WARN; l2_undeclared means neither the catalog nor the purchase row of the latest delivery gives an output declaration to check against. l2_conform_no_required_keys next to l2_conform means the declaration marks no key as required, so vet402 checked that the body is a JSON object or array, not which keys it carries. verified_terms.amount is in 6-decimal ledger units: multiply it by 10^12 on BNB Chain and by 10 on Stellar before comparing it with a 402. Every code, its effect and whether the seller can fix it: https://vet402.com/docs/api#reason-codes. Limit of the method: vet402 buys with a fixed, published User-Agent, so a seller could answer vet402 differently from other buyers; other buyers' settlements show that they paid, not that they received, so the decision cannot detect this.

reasons.description: Since 2026-11-15, entries mirroring reason_codes with an English sentence, verdict effect, and purchase or hash links when the record names them.

refunds.description: Since 2026-11-17. For role=payer, refund totals for the seller host of this resource (summed over payTos, same rules as /sellers/[host]); null when unreadable or for role=payee. Does not change the recommendation.

failures_counted.description: Seller-side failures in the window, summed over payTos.

paid_units.description: Amount paid on those failures (6-decimal units, summed).

read_through.description: Latest indexed block time used for the refund window.

refund_rate.description: refunded_units ÷ paid_units; null when nothing was paid.

refunded_units.description: USDC sent back within 30 days (capped at paid_units, summed).

window_days.description: Refund window after a counted failure (30).

registry.description: ERC-8004 Validation Registry write state — anchored | pending | off.

rules_version.description: Version of the decision function that produced this result.

score.description: Present only with `include_score=1` (since 2026-09-29.3; the key is absent otherwise). The transitional 0–100 payee score with `deprecated: true`, `superseded_by: "recommendation"` and a `note`; not used for the decision. May be null (no EVM payTo, or the score could not be read).

spending_halted.description: vet402's own L1 spending halt. This is a fact about the measurer, not about the seller: while it is true no new L1 attempt is signed, so the L1 facts in this document are not today's observation. Sits outside `facts` because it is global, not a property of the subject. It reads true when the flag itself could not be read (a money gate fails closed).

subject.description: The Resource decided on (§5 ids plus the observatory uuid).

verified_pay_to_by_network.description: Since 2026-11-22. The recipients vet402 paid and confirmed delivery to, per chain: one row per network and pay_to (the latest delivered purchase, same predicate as verified_terms, full history), newest first, at most 10. If the network and payTo pair of the 402 you received is not here, vet402 has not verified the recipient on that network. Empty for role=payee and when nothing was ever delivered; XRPL is left out for the same reason as verified_terms.

verified_terms.description: Since 2026-09-29. The terms vet402 actually paid on the last purchase whose delivery it confirmed (settled, 2xx, non-empty body — the facts.l1.n_delivered predicate), over the full history. Null for role=payee, when nothing was ever delivered, and on XRPL until the issuer is recorded. 0x addresses are lowercase. Compare it with the 402 you received before you pay: if the 402's payTo, asset, network or scheme differ from these, or its amount is higher than `amount` (convert the units first, see `amount`), do not pay — an ALLOW is the fact that these terms delivered, not a guarantee for a different recipient or a higher price.

amount.description: Amount paid in vet402's 6-decimal ledger units (integer string), which are not always the asset's own base units. A 402 on BNB Chain (USD1, 18 decimals) or Stellar (USDC, 7 decimals) writes more digits: multiply this value by 10^12 on BNB Chain and by 10 on Stellar before comparing it with the 402.

asset.description: The asset paid (EVM token contract, Solana mint, XRPL RLUSD currency code in hex).

decimals.description: The decimals of `amount` in the ledger: always 6, not the decimals of the asset.

pay_to.description: The recipient paid. EVM addresses lowercase; Solana base58 and XRPL r-addresses as written.

purchase_id.description: Same form as facts.l1.last_purchase_id (`<CAIP-2>:<tx>`); null when the row has no tx.

scheme.description: exact for x402, charge for MPP (Tempo).

verified_at.description: When that purchase was made (ISO 8601 UTC).

cacheExpiresAt.description: When this verdict stops being the current answer.

degraded.description: True when the verdict was computed with an input that could not be read. Fail-closed: such a verdict is not cached and the SDK and middleware deny on it.

EndpointRef.description: §5 Endpoint / Resource record as returned by the resolve family.

details.description: Present for `invalid_request` — Zod validation error detail (flattened).

documentation.description: On a 401: where the API is documented.

error.description:
Stable machine-readable error code. Request/body validation failures
(malformed JSON, failed schema checks, empty/oversized batches, etc.)
always use `invalid_request`.

reason.description: Present for `attestation_unverifiable` — human-readable reason the on-chain check failed.

signup.description: On a 401: where to get a key.

Evidence.description: One row of evidence. A row is ONE source's observation: counts from different ledgers are never added into a single number, and a row never carries material from two sources. `/decision` and `/observatory/endpoints/{id}/facts` only ever emit `source: vet402`; rows with `source: subgraph` are added to the same array by the payOrRefuse SDK when the caller reads The Graph with their own Graph Gateway API key. vet402 does not proxy that read.

block.description: source: subgraph only - the block the index was read at. `block.number` together with `deployment` is the only self-evident proof that live data was read rather than a static snapshot.

content_type.description: Since 2026-09-29.3, L2 mismatch rows only. The Content-Type of that response, when recorded (60 characters at most).

deployment.description: source: subgraph only - the deployment hash that answered.

mismatch_kind.description: Since 2026-09-29.3, L2 mismatch rows only. missing_keys — the declared required keys named in missing_keys were absent (a BLOCK). unexplained — no missing key on record, so vet402 cannot say what differed (reason code l2_mismatch_unexplained, a WARN).

queriedAt.description: source: subgraph only - when the query ran.

receipts.description: source: subgraph only - how many receipts THAT source knows about (role RECIPIENT). Never added to vet402's own delivery count: the two number different things.

source.description: Which ledger this row was observed in. `vet402` is our own L0-L2 measurement record; `subgraph` is The Graph's x402 subgraph, read by the caller. The SDK's `policy.evidence.source` accepts a third value, `both`, but that says which sources to READ - it is never the source of a row, because a row from "both" would be two ledgers merged into one.

subgraphId.description: source: subgraph only - the subgraph that was queried on The Graph's decentralised network.

EvidenceAge.description: Last delivery timing from paid tests with a freshness tier, recommendation cap, and readable summary.

fresh_within_days.description: Day count through which delivery reads as fresh tier (7).

stale_after_days.description: Day count after which delivery reads as stale and caps at WARN (30).

text.description: One English sentence with the delivery date and days since.

L0Accuracy.description: §12 L0 false-fail / false-pass over the last 7 days. Rates are null below min_sample.

false_fail.description: Published fail that flipped to pass within 7 days.

false_pass.description: Published pass followed by a non-402 answer.

L0PublishedVerdict.description:
Public word in the L0 CSV column `published_verdict`. `pass` is a
latest probe that passed. `fail` is the newest 2 probes both failed
on a route the catalog still lists. `withdrawn` is those same two
failing probes on a route absent from a complete catalog fetch, and
that row is left out of the public L0 fail count. `unverified` is
anything else, including no probe.

L2Status.description: The decision document and the facts document store conform, mismatch, undeclared, or not_checked. The ledger column l2_schema stores match, mismatch, no_declaration, or not_checked. conform is written when the re-read L2 value (l2_reading) of the latest delivery is match. mismatch is written when that re-read value is mismatch. An older mismatch row with no recorded reason is re-read first, and a cut body reads not_checked. In the other cases the decision word is not_checked when the current declaration names output (a required key or an example property), or when the purchase row of the latest delivery recorded a declaration and its re-read value is not_checked, and undeclared when neither holds. The latest delivery is read at any age, so a mismatch holds until a later delivery replaces it; facts.l2.observed_at says when.

endpoints.description: Number of endpoints (or resources) naming this payee.

degraded.description:
**Read this before you act on `recommendation`.** True when at least one input could not be read at all, so this body is a fail-closed refusal, not a measurement. `dataDepth` answers "how much history does this wallet have?"; this answers "did we manage to look?".
A client MUST NOT treat a `degraded: true` body as ALLOW, whatever `recommendation` and `score` say. The engine already forces BLOCK here and refuses to cache the verdict; @vet402/sdk (SpendGuard, `payee_score_degraded`) and @vet402/middleware (`score_degraded`) both deny on this field alone, and so does the Python client in the repository (`packages/python-sdk`, not published to PyPI). The `@vouchscore/*` packages are the former, deprecated names of the same npm packages. Always present.

payee.description: Lowercased wallet address that was scored

signalsUnavailable.description:
**Read this before you act on `recommendation`.** Every input that could not be read on this request, named — currently one or more of `wallet_metrics`, `native_drain`, `usdc_drain`, `outcome_history`. Empty means the whole assessment was measured. Treat the list as open: new input names may be added without a breaking change.
Non-empty with `degraded: false` is the partial-measurement case: the score IS backed by real measurements, just not all of them, and it has been capped below ALLOW for exactly that reason. A client that must not act on an incomplete view MUST NOT treat a body with a non-empty `signalsUnavailable` as ALLOW — SpendGuard denies it as `payee_partial_measurement` and the middleware as `partial_measurement`. Always present (empty array when clean).

drainPattern.description: Exit-scam-shaped check — received funds, then pulled out (near-)everything

drainRatio.description: outgoing / (outgoing + current balance) over the wallet's recent transactions

unmeasured.description: Asset legs that could NOT be read on this request, named rather than averaged away — e.g. ["native_drain"], ["usdc_drain"], or both. Empty when every leg was assessed. These names also appear in the top-level `signalsUnavailable`; a non-empty list means the drain view is partial.

outcomeHistory.description: Prior verdict_outcomes labels naming this wallet (auto-detected or partner-reported)

adjustment.description: Net point adjustment applied to the pre-outcome weighted score

receiving.description: Settlement history where this wallet was the payee (attested via POST /payments/x402)

l1DeliveryCount.description: vet402 2026-08-14 — delivery-verified L1 receipts behind the receiving score (the premium signal: the observatory actually paid this payee and checked what came back). 0 until the observatory writes its first row for this wallet.

l1NonDeliveryReason.description: Present when a non-delivery ceiling was applied to the final score. null when no such ceiling applies.

l1NonSettlingDays.description: Distinct UTC days on which a non-settling paid attempt occurred. Separates a one-day outage from a sustained pattern.

l1PaidNeverSettled.description: Paid attempts by vet402 that resolved WITHOUT an on-chain settlement. Pending verifications are not counted here.

l1PendingVerification.description: Paid attempts whose claimed settlement vet402 has not re-read on-chain yet. Never counted against the payee.

l1Settled.description: Settlements to this payee that vet402 confirmed on-chain (recipient, amount, token, chain, confirmations).

walletHealth.description: Reused from the same on-chain wallet-age/tx-count/burner heuristics as the seller-side score

PayeeVerdictFast.description:
verify-at-settle answer. **Only `hit` + `ALLOW` clears a payment.**
`cache_cold` is the ABSENCE of a verdict, not a permissive one — treat
it as not-ALLOW, warm asynchronously via the full `/score` endpoint
(same cache, TTL 5 min), and retry. See docs/verify-at-settle.md; the
rule is implemented as `payeeVerdictFastAllows` in @vet402/sdk.

This body deliberately carries no `degraded` / `signalsUnavailable`:
the engine never pins a degraded or partially-measured reading, so a
`hit` cannot be a fail-closed refusal wearing an ALLOW.

recommendation.description: Always null — nothing was pinned. NOT an allow.

warmVia.description: Full-score path to call fire-and-forget to warm the same cache

cacheExpiresAt.description: When this pinned verdict stops being the current answer. Clients gating money should re-check it rather than assume the server filtered expired entries (it does — this is belt and braces).

handlerMicros.description: In-handler microseconds spent (a cache read plus JSON)

ReasonEvidenceRef.description: Typed link to a purchase row, chain transaction, content hash, or observatory record.

ReasonExplanation.description: One reason code with its English sentence, verdict effect, recommendation cap, and evidence links.

max_recommendation.description: The best verdict this reason alone would allow.

text.description: One English sentence for this reason code.

ResolveResult.description: §7.3. `query.kind` says how `q` was read; the optional keys follow from it — url → resource + endpoints, domain → endpoints, address / payee_id → endpoints + payees, tx → settlement (+ resource when attributed). Measurement identifiers only, never a recommendation.

not_found.description: Present only when `query.kind` is url, domain, address or payee_id and nothing was found; `endpoints` is then an empty array. `reason` is `not_in_catalog`: the catalog is read from public x402 discovery listings, so an endpoint missing from it has not been measured, which is not a finding about it. `next` links to the API reference. `listing_sources` names each source vet402 reads listings from, with the UTC times its syncs start (the field was added on 2026-10-21). A CDP Bazaar sync that stops early adds the pages it read and not the rest. The Circle x402 discovery is read on the same run as the MPP directory. There is no application or fee. `documentation` links to the FAQ section on why an endpoint is not listed and how a listing gets into the CDP Bazaar and the Circle x402 discovery.

sync_times_utc.description: Times of day (UTC, HH:MM) when a sync of this source starts.

settlement_not_found.description: Present only when `query.kind` is `tx` and no settlement was found. Raw settlement rows are kept for a 7-day window; older days are folded into daily (payee, payer) aggregates, so census counts stay exact while individual receipts are no longer stored. Absence of a settlement therefore does not mean the transaction never happened.

ResourceSubject.description: The Resource a facts / decision document is about (§5 ids plus the observatory uuid).

id.description: resource_id (sha256 hex) when the catalog has one.

ScoreBreakdown.description: N-21 explainability. Decomposition of the chain score into its four weighted components plus the sybil adjustment — the exact arithmetic of the weighting, so it cannot disagree with trustScore. Omitted on hard-blocked verdicts where no weighting ran. The manual whitelist/ blacklist layer is intentionally excluded (see manualOverride).

prePolicyScore.description: weightedSubtotal + sybilPenalty, clamped; equals trustScore unless a manual list moved it

sybilPenalty.description: Points removed by sybil/availability flags (<= 0); see signals.sybil.flags

weightedSubtotal.description: Weighted average of the four components before the sybil penalty

contribution.description: score × weight ÷ 0.8; the four contributions sum to weightedSubtotal

score.description: 0-100 component score fed into the weighting

weight.description: Its weight in the chain-signal sum (identity 0.2 / reputation 0.3 / wallet 0.2 / x402 0.1)

Carried by every 0–100 score response since 2026-09-29. The score
itself is unchanged; this says it is deprecated and what to call instead.

rules_version.description: Decision rules version (DECISION_RULES_VERSION) for the deprecated score.

SellerFacts.description: §8.1 seller facts for a Resource / Endpoint / Payee. Measurement records only — no trustScore, no recommendation (§8.3).

l1.description: Counts are over the 30-day window, except last_attempt_at, which reads the full history.

last_attempt_at.description: When vet402 last attempted an L1 purchase against this resource (ISO 8601 UTC; null before the first attempt). Distinct from observed_at, which is when we last *paid*: an attempt that ended before the signature (no eligible accept, over cap, spending halted) still sets this. Over the full history, not the 30-day window, so an older attempt does not read as "never attempted".

n_inconclusive.description: Signed paid attempts held rather than counted against the seller: the paid request answered 4xx and the payment settled (since 2026-09-08); the paid request answered a 4xx other than 402 with no settlement receipt, or answered 402 or 5xx between 2026-09-13T00:00Z and 2026-09-15T23:49Z while vet402's own Base payer wallet was out of USDC (both since 2026-09-17). Counted in n_attempts (and in n_settled when settled) — the same set the per-endpoint purchases route reports as inconclusiveCount — and held out of the delivery judgement. The decision counts n_attempts − l1_basis.n_not_counted (n_not_counted includes these rows and, since 2026-09-29, the attempts named by the l1_not_counted_* reason codes); when that is 0 the reason code is l1_inconclusive (a gap in our measurement, not evidence against the seller), so l1_inconclusive can appear with n_inconclusive 0.

n_probe_error.description: Deprecated 2026-09-08 — same value as n_inconclusive, kept for clients that read the old name. Before that date these rows were excluded from n_attempts, which published a seller with ten settled purchases as l1_not_attempted.

l2.description: §6.3 — a mismatch is published with the declaration hash, the response hash and a diff hash (sha256 of {declaration_hash, response_hash, missing}) plus the missing keys; never the paid body itself. response_hash is present for conform too. settlement_30d_test.description: Of raw, wallets vet402 pays from (wash_flag test). Left out of the wash_dominated denominator. Other measurement services are settlement_30d_measurement.

wash_dominated.description: Real demand is near zero while listings are thick (§8.3 BLOCK condition). Denominator is third-party raw (raw minus test minus measurement).

SettlementRef.description: One indexed settlement (§7.2), with its attribution and wash flag.

block_time_source.description: Clock behind block_time. chain is the ledger time stored at verification, or the block time on the observed purchase recorded for that verification when the purchase row did not store one. attempted_at is the purchase attempt time, used when no ledger time was stored. verified_at marks an older row whose block_time is the time verification finished. null when the row names none of these clocks.

SloSnapshot.description: §14 operator SLOs. A metric that could not be measured is null and is named in `unmeasured`.

l1_7d.description:
Counts behind `l1_probe_error_rate_pct`, and the held rows of the
same 7 days, so the three similar-sounding figures can be told
apart. `attempts`: every L1 row attempted in the last 7 days, any
status. `request_errors`: of those, `request_error` or
`in_flight`. `signed`: of those, rows where vet402 signed a payment
(settled, settle_failed, delivered_no_receipt,
settle_claimed_unverifiable, settle_claimed, settle_claim_refuted).
`held`: of the signed rows, those with a `held_reason` in the
ledger export. Since 2026-09-29.

l1_probe_error_rate_pct.description:
`l1_7d.request_errors` / `l1_7d.attempts`, in percent: L1 attempts
in the last 7 days whose purchase run did not complete inside
vet402 (status `request_error`, or `in_flight` left unfinished).
Not the held share of the ledger export and not the "vet402's
side" column of /sellers, which count different things.

agentId.description: ERC-8004 agent ID; "0" if wallet-only lookup

blockReason.description: Present when recommendation is BLOCK (e.g. wallet_mismatch, operator_policy)

indexedAgentRows.description: Agent rows the owner indexer currently holds

lastBlock.description: Last block the owner indexer has processed (decimal string); null when unknown

manualOverride.description: True when customer WL/BL changed the recommendation

reasons.description: Stable machine-readable codes behind the verdict, derived from the same signals (for integrators' compliance logs). Cannot disagree with the recommendation.

hasMetadataUri.description: Whether the agent has a metadata URI on-chain (not a validation of URI contents)

onChainAvgScore.description: Raw on-chain reputation average before normalization

l1PurchaseCount.description: vet402 2026-08-14 — delivery-verified L1 observed purchases behind the axis score (the premium signal). 0 until the observatory writes its first row for this wallet.

score.description: Internal 0–100 component for the highest-weighted axis. vet402 2026-08-14: the axis is "verifiable economic activity", not x402 settlements alone — this reflects the STRONGER of the L1 observed purchases below and the x402 settlements above. pay_to.description: The recipient paid. EVM addresses lowercase; Solana base58 as written.

active.description: Set false automatically after 20 consecutive failed deliveries

WebhookDelivery.description: The JSON body POSTed to your endpoint. Signed with header `Vouch-Signature: t=<unix>,v1=<hex HMAC-SHA256 of "<t>.<rawBody>">`. Verify by recomputing the HMAC with your whsec_ secret in constant time and rejecting a timestamp more than 300s old (replay guard). Delivery is at-most-once (no retry); dedupe on `id`.

Scores themselves are never pushed.

info.description:
Independent verification for the x402 agent-payment economy. Scores payee
wallets and ERC-8004 agents on Base, returns a 0-100 score with an
ALLOW/WARN/BLOCK recommendation, and publishes what happened after those
verdicts.

**Disclaimer:** Scores are informational only and do not constitute a guarantee,
credit assessment, or investment advice. Every response that carries a score or
a published rate carries its own `disclaimer` string in the payload, so the
caveat travels with the number.

**Rate limits.** Authenticated calls: a per-account monthly quota (Free 3,000
/ Pro 50,000 / Scale 500,000), shared across keys, reset at the UTC month
boundary. Each `/score` is 1 unit; a `/scores/batch` of N agents is N units.
Scored responses carry `X-RateLimit-Limit`, `X-RateLimit-Used`, and
`X-RateLimit-Remaining`. There is no per-second burst throttle on
authenticated calls — you may spend the quota as fast as you like; a `429`
with `Retry-After` means the monthly quota is exhausted. Separate IP-based
abuse throttles (e.g. 60 auth-failures/min/IP) exist only to blunt
key-guessing and scraping and are not hit by valid authenticated traffic.

Key-less calls are throttled per IP instead. Every response on those paths
carries `RateLimit-Limit` — the ceiling for that path, true for every caller.
`RateLimit-Remaining` and `RateLimit-Reset` (IETF draft names, distinct from
the `X-RateLimit-*` monthly quota above) are per-caller counters and are sent
only on responses a shared cache does not replay to a different caller —
chiefly the `429`, which also carries `Retry-After`. A CDN-cached `200`
deliberately omits them: a counter belonging to whoever populated the cache
would be a number that means something other than what it appears to mean.

**Unknown paths.** Any request under `/api/` that matches no route answers
`404` with a JSON body (`{"error":"not_found","path":…}`), never an HTML
page — a mistyped path is safe to feed to the same parser as every other
response.

post.description:
Since 2026-10-28. A Model Context Protocol server over Streamable HTTP.
`https://vet402.com/mcp` is rewritten to this path. Read only, free and
key-less. It serves protocol revision `2025-06-18` (with `initialize`)
and `2026-07-28` (stateless, `server/discover`) from the same URL and
keeps no session. The body is a single JSON-RPC 2.0 message.

Tools (all with `readOnlyHint: true`, `destructiveHint: false`,
`idempotentHint: true`, `openWorldHint: false` and an `outputSchema`):
`check_x402_seller` (what happened when vet402 paid an x402 URL, with
the transaction of each attempt), `check_my_x402_endpoint` (the public
seller page of a host, the catalogs it is listed in and when vet402 can
buy again), `find_x402_sellers` (listings matching a query with the same
Wilson ranking as GET /api/v1/find), `check_payment_proof` (chain read
of a payment), and `check_8004_agent` (ERC-8004 feedback proof
re-read, same JSON as GET /api/v1/erc8004/check). Each tool
result carries `as_of` and `method_url`. `check_x402_seller` and
`check_my_x402_endpoint` also carry `record_url` at the top level, and
`find_x402_sellers` carries it per row. Each result is
returned as `structuredContent` and as the same JSON in a text block.

Limits: 120 requests per minute per IP (`MCP_RATE_PER_MIN`), 30 per
minute per IP for `find_x402_sellers` (`MCP_FIND_RATE_PER_MIN`) and
30 per         minute per IP for `check_my_x402_endpoint`
(`MCP_SELLER_RATE_PER_MIN`), 20 per minute per IP for `check_payment_proof`
(shared with POST /api/v1/payment-proof), and 30 per minute per IP for
`check_8004_agent` (shared with GET /api/v1/erc8004/check), each on top of
the first. The
request body is capped at 64 KB and JSON-RPC batches are refused.
The server reads only its own database and makes no outbound request,
except `check_8004_agent`, which reads the public ERC-8004 registry over RPC
and the feedback's public https feedbackURI (no redirects, 256 KB cap).
Calls are counted per client kind and UTC day in `client_usage_daily`
(routes `mcp:initialize`, `mcp:check_x402_seller`,
`mcp:check_my_x402_endpoint`, `mcp:find_x402_sellers`). Those counts
hold the UTC day, the route, the client kind and the number, with no
URL, User-Agent text or IP address. The IP address (an IPv6 address
cut to its /64) is held in the rate-limit store for the one-minute
window, and the daily log purge deletes the expired rows.

200.description:
A JSON-RPC 2.0 response, as `application/json` or as a single
`text/event-stream` message (2025-06-18 clients that accept it).

202.description: A JSON-RPC notification was accepted. No body.

400.description:
The body is a JSON-RPC batch (`error.message: batch_not_supported`)
or is not a valid MCP message (JSON-RPC error from the MCP library).

403.description:
`forbidden`. The request carries an `Origin` header that is not
vet402.com. Requests without `Origin` (server to server) pass.
No CORS headers are sent.

413.description: The body is larger than 64 KB (JSON-RPC error, `error.message` is `request_too_large`).

429.description:
Rate limited. The body is a JSON-RPC error with `code: -32029`,
`message: rate_limited` and `data.retry_after_s`. `Retry-After` and
`RateLimit-*` headers are set.

503.description:
`mcp_disabled` when the entry is switched off (`MCP_ENABLED=false`),
or `temporarily_unavailable` with `Retry-After: 30` when the
database or the rate-limit store cannot be read.

whether vet402 has censored an address and on what grounds, and dispute

get.description:
What happened AFTER the verdicts vet402 issued, over a rolling 90-day
window: aggregate counts only — no wallet addresses, no agent ids, no
per-customer data. Key-less on purpose, because an accuracy number shown
selectively is marketing rather than measurement.

Two partitioned sets. The top-level figures are **external usage**:
verdicts API users requested, judged by what the wallet did next.
`operatorBenchmark` is a **self-seeded** controlled test against a fixed,
versioned set of publicly-labelled addresses; it is excluded from every
external figure at the SQL layer, so it cannot pad them.

`interpretation` carries, in machine-readable form, the same caveats the
human page prints next to these numbers — a "detection" counts BLOCK
*or* WARN, a 0% false-positive rate means "none were blocked" rather
than "all were passed", and a rate below the minimum sample is `null`
rather than a number computed from noise. Read the JSON alone and you
have the whole disclosure; you are not expected to parse the HTML.

Rates move as the sample grows: cite them with `generatedAt`.

Product spec §12 (2026-09-02) adds the measuring instrument's own
quality: `l0` (false-fail rate = published fails overturned to pass
within 7 days, target < 3%; false-pass rate = published passes whose
next probe was no_402, target < 2%; null below the minimum sample),
`slo` (L1 probe-error rate, C1 L0 freshness within 36h, C2 L1
freshness within 48h, reverse-lookup latency within 60s, published
failure evidence completeness — unmeasured items are named in
`slo.unmeasured`), and `coverageWeekly` (listed / L0 measured / L1
measured / real and raw settlements over 7 days).

get.description:
Returns the exact message the agent's on-chain wallet must sign to
register a passport, with that wallet resolved from the ERC-8004
registry, plus the `issued` timestamp embedded in it (echo it back in
the POST). The message binds agentId + wallet + name, optionally a
`url` line, and an `issued` line (replay guard). `issued` must be
within 10 minutes of the server clock at POST time. Key-less; 30
requests per minute per IP.

**Message form changed 2026-09-05 (S-6).** Every signed message now
opens with `vet402.com — <purpose>` and carries a `domain: vet402.com`
line, so the wallet's signing view shows which site is asking; the
`issued` line states its own `(valid 10 minutes)`; and the last line
says what the signature does and that it moves no funds. Signatures
over the pre-2026-09-05 form are still accepted until
**2026-09-21T00:00:00Z** (the response carries `legacy_message: true`);
after that they are refused with `signature_message_legacy_expired`
rather than a bare `signature_mismatch`. Always fetch the current
message from the GET preview instead of building it locally.

writes are monotonic on `issued` (an older signature returns `409

post.description:
Permissionless L0 contribution intake (Phase 3.3 v0), OFF by default
behind an operator flag. Submissions are EIP-191 signed over the
canonical message — since 2026-09-05 a human-readable, newline-joined
block rather than one colon-packed line, so the signer can read which
endpoint and which verdict they are attesting to:

```
vet402.com — external observation
domain: vet402.com
endpoint: {endpointId}
verdict: {verdict}
http status: {httpStatus, or "not reported"}
latency: {latencyMs} ms
issued: {issued} (valid 10 minutes)
Recorded in the public ledger. Not counted in the published verdict (v0).
```

The message that verified is stored verbatim for auditability.

**Breaking change 2026-08-22 (v0 → v1).** `issued` (RFC 3339 UTC, e.g.
`2026-08-22T13:04:05Z`) is now part of the signed message and is
REQUIRED. The server rejects a signature whose `issued` is more than
10 minutes from server time in either direction (400
`signature_expired`), and rejects a repeat of the same canonical
message (409 `replayed`). Without both checks a captured signature
could be replayed indefinitely. Signatures produced against the v0
message form no longer verify.

**Message form changed 2026-09-05 (S-6).** Every signed message now
opens with `vet402.com — <purpose>` and carries a `domain: vet402.com`
line, so the wallet's signing view shows which site is asking; the
`issued` line states its own `(valid 10 minutes)`; and the last line
says what the signature does and that it moves no funds. Signatures
over the pre-2026-09-05 form are still accepted until
**2026-09-21T00:00:00Z** (the response carries `legacy_message: true`);
after that they are refused with `signature_message_legacy_expired`
rather than a bare `signature_mismatch`. Always fetch the current
message from the GET preview instead of building it locally.
v0 contributions are NEVER folded into published verdicts — the public
register remains computed from vet402's own probes until the weighted
v1 design ships. IP-throttled to 10/min.

signature.description: EIP-191 signature of the canonical message

400.description: Invalid input, invalid signature, or `signature_expired` (the signed `issued` is outside the 10-minute window)

409.description: `replayed` — this exact canonical message was already accepted

get.description:
Product spec §10. Every row is a published verdict that was later
overturned or completed: `dispute_remeasure` (a seller's signed dispute
triggered a re-measurement over a separate path that overturned the
verdict), `settlement_backfill` (a claimed settlement was later
confirmed or refuted on-chain), `reverify` (a C4 re-verification).
`before` / `after` are the published values. Corrections unfavourable
to vet402 are listed the same way; rows are never deleted. Key-less; 60/min.

Since 2026-09-29 every row can be read: a page holds at most 500
rows, `page.nextCursor` pages back to the oldest row (null on the last
page), and `total` is the number of rows matching `endpoint` and
`reason`, whatever the cursor. The two counts in the header of
`/corrections` are `total` split by reason: "Ledger status changes"
is `?reason=settlement_backfill`, "Corrections" is the hand-written
entries plus every other reason. For a `purchase` row, `subject_id`
is the `purchase_id` column of `/api/v1/observatory/export.csv`.
`settlement_path` names the path a `settlement_backfill` row took,
worked out from `before` / `after` when the row is read (stored values
are not changed): `verified_settled`, `claim_refuted`,
`seller_named_tx_promoted` (the seller named the transaction in its
payment response although its receipt did not say success; `before`
and `after` carry the same seller-named hash, and the export keeps
`settlement_source=seller_claim`), `vet402_index_link`,
`late_link_withdrawn`, `seller_named_tx_declined` or `other`. The
`definition` field of the response spells each one out.

get.description:
One row per `settled` purchase in the time window, with the three
delivery values discussed for x402 buyers (`delivered`,
`no_body_observed`, `not_established`) plus the raw ledger fields
needed to re-count them. The population is `settled` rows only. The
three values sum to the `settled` rows in the file, and `delivered`
uses the same rule as `l1.delivered` on `/api/v1/observatory/state`.
The counts are not expected to equal the state totals. State counts
the whole ledger, not the `days` window. The file can stop at 50,000
rows. The two are cached on separate schedules. A correction can
change a row between the two reads. The frozen ledger export at
`/api/v1/observatory/export.csv` is unchanged.

`days` follows the same rules as the ledger export. It is a decimal
integer. A value outside 1..366 or with leading zeros is answered with a 308 to
the canonical `?days=` (`90.5` or `1e2` are 400 `invalid_days`). Any
other query parameter, or `days` given twice, is 400 `invalid_query`.
Output truncates at 50,000 rows (`x-vet402-truncated`). IP-throttled to
6/min. Reads the store one export at a time across all callers (503

post.description:
Only the holder of the endpoint's payTo key can dispute its record.
Since 2026-09-05 the signed message carries the first 200 characters of
`reason` in plain text alongside its sha256, so the dispute is no
longer a blind signature, and states that the re-measurement publishes
either way:

```
vet402.com — measurement dispute
domain: vet402.com
endpoint: {endpointId}
subject: {subject}
reason (first 200 chars): {reason, control characters flattened to spaces}
reason sha256: {sha256(reason)}
issued: {issued} (valid 10 minutes)
Filing this will trigger a re-measurement whose result is published, including if it confirms the original verdict.
```

Acceptance triggers one real L0 re-measurement recorded through the
normal publication gate. Records are never deleted on dispute. 5/min.

**Breaking change 2026-08-22 (v0 → v1).** `issued` (RFC 3339 UTC) is
now part of the signed message and is REQUIRED. A signature whose
`issued` is more than 10 minutes from server time in either direction
is rejected (400 `signature_expired`), and a repeat of the same
canonical message is rejected (409 `replayed`) — otherwise a captured
signature could be replayed to trigger unlimited live re-probes.
Signatures produced against the v0 message form no longer verify.

**Message form changed 2026-09-05 (S-6).** Every signed message now
opens with `vet402.com — <purpose>` and carries a `domain: vet402.com`
line, so the wallet's signing view shows which site is asking; the
`issued` line states its own `(valid 10 minutes)`; and the last line
says what the signature does and that it moves no funds. Signatures
over the pre-2026-09-05 form are still accepted until
**2026-09-21T00:00:00Z** (the response carries `legacy_message: true`);
after that they are refused with `signature_message_legacy_expired`
rather than a bare `signature_mismatch`. Always fetch the current
message from the GET preview instead of building it locally.

issued.description: RFC 3339 UTC instant folded into the signed message. Must be within 10 minutes of server time in either direction. Required since 2026-08-22 (message form v1).

400.description: Invalid input, invalid signature, or `signature_expired` (signed `issued` outside the 10-minute window)

409.description: `replayed` — this exact canonical message was already accepted

get.description:
One row per attempt that reached a decision, as CSV — a portable audit
trail (Phase 4.2 v0). Paid attempts are the rows with status settled,
settle_failed, delivered_no_receipt, settle_claimed,
settle_claimed_unverifiable or settle_claim_refuted (their count is
`l1.attempts`); the other rows stopped before signing, with
`spent_units` 0 and a blank `network`. No new claims are minted here:
rows are the ledger facts (attempted_at, resource_key, network,
status, amounts, tx_hash, delivery figures). Excludes vet402-side
non-events (budget_denied / halted / request_error / in_flight). `days`
is a decimal integer; a value outside 1..366 or with leading zeros is
answered with a 308 to the canonical `?days=` (since 2026-09-29;
`90.5` or `1e2` are 400 `invalid_days`). Any other query parameter,
or `days` given twice, is 400 `invalid_query` (since 2026-09-29).
Optional `include=erc8004_agent` (since 2026-11-17) appends one column at
the end; any other `include` value is 400 `invalid_include`. Output
truncates at 50,000 rows and says so in
the `x-vet402-truncated` header. IP-throttled to 6/min. The three CSV
exports read the store one at a time across all callers; a request
that finds another export running gets 503 `export_busy` with
`Retry-After` (since 2026-09-29). A cell whose text starts with `=`,
`+`, `-`, `@`, a tab or a carriage return is written with a leading
`'` so a spreadsheet reads it as text (numbers are left as they are;
since 2026-09-29; the same holds for the other two exports).

Columns, in order (columns are only ever appended; existing names,
order and meaning do not change): `attempted_at`, `resource_key`,
`network`, `status`, `amount_units`, `spent_units`, `tx_hash`,
`http_status_paid`, `latency_ms`, `l2_schema`, `held_reason`
(since 2026-09-17), `request_body`, `request_body_sha256`,
`settlement_source` (since 2026-09-20), `request_query`,
`request_query_sha256` (since 2026-09-21), `confirmed_units`
(since 2026-09-29), `purchase_id` (since 2026-09-29), `l2_reading`
(since 2026-09-29), `response_sha256`, `response_bytes` (since 2026-11-24).
With `?include=erc8004_agent`, one more column is appended:
`erc8004_agent` (since 2026-11-17).

vet402 keeps `auth_nonce` on purchase rows for purchases it signs
itself (EIP-3009 / memo binding). That value is internal to the
ledger and is not a column in this export. `@vet402/sdk` carries an
authorization nonce in the payment it signs; the observatory does not
ingest that field from clients—it is not stored or replayed.

- `amount_units` — the price the seller's 402 asked for, in vet402's
  6-decimal ledger units (the asset's base units on most chains; USD1
  on BNB Chain has 18 decimals and USDC on Stellar 7).
- `spent_units` — the amount vet402 signed for on this attempt: what
  it put at stake, not an amount shown to have moved. A
  `settle_failed` row with no `tx_hash` still carries the price here.
  Read `confirmed_units` for money that moved. The meaning of this
  column has not changed; the note is new.
- `confirmed_units` — the amount vet402 re-read on-chain as
  transferred: equal to `spent_units` on `settled` rows and `0` on
  every other row, including `settle_claimed` rows that are still
  awaiting the re-read (they take the amount once they turn
  `settled`). `0` means no transfer vet402 has confirmed, not a
  transfer shown not to have happened. The response also carries
  both definitions in the `x-vet402-column-notes` header, because a
  CSV has nowhere to put a comment.

- `held_reason` — why the row is held rather than counted against the
  seller: `settled_4xx`, `unsettled_4xx`, `payer_unfunded`; blank when
  the row is counted.
- `request_body` — what the paid request carried: `declared` (the body
  the seller's own 402 declares in `extensions.bazaar.info.input.body`,
  sent unedited; since 2026-09-17), `empty` (`{}`), `operator_example`
  (since 2026-11-22: a seller vet402 added itself, source `operator`, whose
  402 declares no body; vet402 sent the example body written in
  src/lib/observatory/operator-listings.ts), `pay_skills_example`
  (since 2026-11-24: pay.sh delivery targets, source `pay_skills`,
  src/lib/observatory/pay-skills-listings-data.ts), `none` (a request
  formed with no body, whether or not it reached the seller; recorded
  since 2026-09-20). Blank means the row
  holds no record: rows before 2026-09-17, bodiless requests before
  2026-09-20, and rows that ended before a paid request went out.
  Blank is not `empty`. The row does not record the HTTP method, so
  older rows are not back-filled.
- `request_body_sha256` — on `declared` rows since 2026-09-20 (and on `operator_example` rows), the
  lowercase hex SHA-256 of the exact bytes sent (the declared body
  passed through `JSON.stringify`). The body itself is not
  republished; it is the seller's text and the seller's 402 serves it
  to anyone. Blank otherwise.
- `settlement_source` — who named `tx_hash`: `seller_claim` (the paid
  response carried a settlement receipt naming it), `vet402_index`
  (no receipt came back; vet402's own settlements index found the
  transfer by payer, payee, exact amount and time window, and the row
  then went through the same on-chain re-read), or `circle_gateway`
  (a Circle Gateway batch transaction stored beside the row). This value is absent while the Arc Gateway lane flag is off. That
  value can be set when `tx_hash` is empty, because the batch
  transaction is not the row's own `tx_hash`. Blank when the row has
  no `tx_hash` and no Circle Gateway batch transaction. The settled
  count of `vet402_index` rows is `l1.settledLateLinked` on
  `/api/v1/observatory/state`.
- `request_query` — which URL the paid request went to: `declared`
  (the query arguments the seller's own 402 declares in
  `extensions.bazaar.info.input.queryParams`, appended to the listed
  URL as declared), `empty` (the seller declared none), `refused` (a
  declaration was there and vet402's own rules did not use it — a
  non-scalar value, an empty name, over the caps, declared names that
  collide once folded, a host or path that would move, or a collision
  with names the listed URL already carries that left nothing to
  append). A declared name the listed URL already carries is dropped
  on its own: the listing's query stands and the declaration's other
  pairs are still appended, so that row is `declared` and the hash
  below says what went out. The label has been recorded on the row
  since 2026-09-20 and published as this column since 2026-09-21, on
  the networks named in vet402's per-network allow-list; the paid
  request's URL and the row are unchanged on every other network.
  Blank means the row holds no record: a row on a network the
  allow-list does not name, a Tempo (MPP) row, a row that ended before
  a paid request went out, and rows before 2026-09-20. The column
  alone does not separate those four from one another, and blank is
  not `empty`. Older rows are not back-filled. Within the window the
  response covers, the rows whose `request_query` is not blank are the
  networks this has been in effect on, and the `declared` ones are
  where pairs were actually appended; a network can be on the
  allow-list and carry nothing but `empty` and `refused`.
- `request_query_sha256` — on `declared` rows, the lowercase hex
  SHA-256 of the appended pairs written as one form-urlencoded string:
  the appended pairs alone (neither the query the listed URL already
  carried nor a declared name dropped for colliding with one), in the
  declaration's own key order (integer-like names first, ascending, by
  the JavaScript rule), `application/x-www-form-urlencoded` so a space
  is `+`, `&` between pairs and `=` between name and value, and no
  leading `?` or `&`. The query string itself is not republished: the
  names and values are the seller's own, and the 402 that answered
  vet402's unpaid request is where they were read from. The hash covers the appended pairs alone, not the listed URL or
  which endpoint was bought, so it matches two rows on the same
  endpoint, or a row against a fresh 402; it is not a way of hiding a
  short declared query. Blank otherwise.
- `confirmed_units` — see above: `spent_units` on `settled` rows,
  `0` otherwise.
- `purchase_id` — the purchase's id (a UUID the database assigns to
  each attempt; it carries no payer, payee or amount). It is the
  `subject_id` of that purchase's rows in
  `/api/v1/observatory/corrections` (`subject_type` `purchase`), so a
  ledger status change can be joined to its export row. The rows
  within one `attempted_at` second are ordered by it.
- `l2_reading` — `l2_schema` read again with today's rules: the value
  the record page and the decision's `facts.l2` use. An older row
  whose body was cut at 16,000 bytes reads `not_checked`; a complete
  body that is not valid JSON stays `mismatch`. An older row with no
  recorded reason reads `no_declaration` when the listing declares no
  output now, and `not_checked` when no missing key was recorded and its
  JSON body ran past the stored start. `l2_schema` keeps the value
  recorded at the time.
- `response_sha256` — since 2026-11-24, on rows where vet402 read a
  paid response body, the lowercase hex SHA-256 of the exact byte
  sequence read (UTF-8 bytes as received, before any decode for L2).
  The body itself is not republished. Blank when the row holds no
  record: rows before 2026-11-24 and rows where no paid response body
  was read. Filled only when vet402 read the paid response body
  through to the end (not when the read hit the cap or stopped
  partway).
- `response_bytes` — on rows with `response_sha256`, the length in
  bytes of that same sequence. `0` means an empty body was read
  completely. Blank when the row holds no record. Blank is not `0`.
  Filled only when vet402 read the paid response body through to the
  end (not when the read hit the cap or stopped partway).
- `erc8004_agent` — only when `?include=erc8004_agent` is set: when the
  row's `pay_to` exactly matches the owner or `agentWallet` of an agent
  in vet402's Base ERC-8004 Identity Registry index, the CAIP id
  `eip155:8453:{agentId}`; blank when there is no such match.

`scripts/declared-body-before-after.mjs` recomputes, from this CSV
alone, the paid 2xx rate of the same endpoints before and after the
declared body.

get.description:
Daily rollup of the same raw measurements the Observatory publishes,
keyed by UTC day and chain. `chain` is the network as stored: mostly
CAIP-2, plus the older slugs base, solana and base-sepolia, which mean
the same chains, so fold them before summing. Read by the /observatory/state
history chart from the same reader, so page and API cannot disagree.
Chain "unknown" means neither the payment rail nor the catalog row
declares a network.

`l1Attempts` uses the same paid-attempt denominator as
`/api/v1/observatory/state` (an attempt is a request whose payment was
signed and sent). The rollup is recomputed for the trailing
`recomputeWindowDays` days on every run, so a settlement confirmed
after a day's first rollup is folded in on a later run. Days older than
that window are reconciled when raw L1 totals diverge from the daily
table (up to 10 days per cron run, oldest first). Summing `days` therefore
tracks, but can trail, the live totals in
`/api/v1/observatory/state` — `coverageFrom`, `rolledUpThrough` and
`lastRollupAt` say exactly which span and vintage the sum covers.
Key-less; IP-throttled to 30/min; CDN-cached for 1 hour.

recomputeWindowDays.description: How many trailing days are recomputed from raw on every run. Older days are reconciled when raw L1 totals diverge from the daily table (up to 10 days per cron run).

The per-endpoint data behind the L0 counts of
`/api/v1/observatory/state` (since 2026-09-29): one row per endpoint
on record, active or not, excluding endpoints that pay vet402's own
addresses — the same population and the same rules as the state
figures. Counting `published_verdict=pass` gives `publishedPass`;
adding `listed=true` gives `publishedPassActive`; adding
`latest_probe_older_than_7d=true` gives
`publishedPassActiveProbeOlderThan7d`. Grouping `network_class=mainnet`
rows by `chain` gives `byChain`; `testnet` rows are
`byChainTestnetEndpoints` and `unclassified` rows are
`byChainUnclassified`. The two can differ for a while because the CDN
holds each response separately; compare the retrieval times.

Columns: `endpoint_id`, `resource_key`, `network` (as the catalog
wrote it), `chain` (vet402's label), `network_class` (`mainnet` |

active), `published_verdict` (`pass` = the latest probe passed; `fail` =
the newest 2 probes both failed and the route is still active;
`withdrawn` = those same two failing probes on a route absent from
a complete catalog fetch, left out of the public L0 fail count;
`unverified` = anything else, including no probe; the allowed values
are the `L0PublishedVerdict` enum), `latest_probe_verdict`,
`last_probed_at` (UTC),
`latest_probe_older_than_7d`. The definitions also travel in the
`x-vet402-column-notes` header; the retrieval time in
`x-vet402-retrieved-at`. IP-throttled to 6/min; CDN-cached for up to
15 minutes. Takes no query parameters: any is 400 `invalid_query`
(since 2026-09-29). Reads the store one export at a time across all
callers (503 `export_busy` with `Retry-After`).
