get.description:
Key-less machine-readable twin of the `/observatory/state` page: the
same aggregate figures — endpoints on record, active records,
delisted, published pass/fail/unverified, per-chain breakdown, and L1
real-purchase totals — computed by the same readers so the page and
this API can never disagree. Facts with denominators, no composite
score, no evaluative language. IP-throttled to 30/min; CDN-cached for
15 minutes (the catalog, probe and purchase runs move the figures several times a day).

adoption.description: Use of vet402 by others, each figure with its period, read time and source. sdkDownloads is npm's own last-month window for @vet402/sdk. keyedDecisionCalls repeats the monthly values /api/v1/usage/monthly publishes for key owners outside vet402 (owner_relation external or prezenti_grantee): closed months only, public chains only, groups of 3 or more owners only. A figure that cannot be read or published is left out, field and all. Since 2026-11-08.

byChain.description: L0 per chain, mainnets only (byChainScope): a row appears only for a network id vet402 knows to be a mainnet. Since 2026-09-29 an id vet402 cannot name is left out and listed in byChainUnclassified instead of being assumed to be a mainnet.

chain.description: Join key from the same names as l1.byChain.chain. Unchanged.

label.description: Public name of this chain, from the same list as l1.byChain.label. Screens show this field.

network.description: Canonical CAIP-2 id for this chain, from the same list as l1.byChain.network.

byChainTestnetEndpoints.description: Endpoints on known testnets, left out of byChain. Since 2026-09-29.

byChainUnclassified.description: Network ids vet402 cannot name as a mainnet or a testnet, verbatim, with their endpoint counts; left out of byChain. sum(byChain.totalEndpoints) + byChainTestnetEndpoints + sum(byChainUnclassified.totalEndpoints) = totalEndpoints. Since 2026-09-29.

catalogSnapshots.description: The latest snapshot of each discovery catalog vet402 reads (cdp_bazaar, circle_discovery, mpp_directory), plus `operator` for the checked-in list of sellers vet402 adds itself, sorted by source. `complete` says whether the fetch of THAT catalog alone counts as complete; fetchedCount can be below totalCount on a complete fetch.

complete.description: Whether the fetch counts as complete. Null with no record.

cursorPassCompleted.description: cdp_bazaar only: whether the cursor read has closed a full pass.

totalCount.description: The total the catalog reported at that fetch. It is not the count of active listings.

cdpBazaarIngestStale.description: True when the last closed strong pass of the CDP Bazaar read is older than 36 hours.

cdpBazaarLastStrongPassAt.description: When that pass closed. Null when none has.

coverage7d.description: The share of active endpoints with an L0 probe from the last 7 days.

erc8004.description: Exact address matches between the payTo of vet402's purchase rows and the owner (or agentWallet) of an ERC-8004 agent in vet402's Identity Registry index. Lowercase address equality only, no name or fuzzy matching. Read from vet402's own index, cached for 5 minutes, with its own readAt. status unavailable carries no counts. The top-level counts are Base. byChain gives Base, Ethereum and BNB Chain each on its own. A chain whose index cannot be read says unavailable with a reason, never 0. Since 2026-11-08. Ethereum and BNB Chain since 2026-11-10.

about.description: One line on what is counted

indexBlock.description: The last block this chain's index has read and written. Present only when scanned.

reason.description: Present only when unavailable. index_not_started when the index has not read this chain yet.

scannedAgents.description: Agents with an owner in this chain's index. Present only when scanned.

byChain.description: "eip155:8453", "eip155:1" and "eip155:56". Each is scanned (with scannedAgents, matchedAgents and indexBlock) or unavailable (with reason and no counts). agentId is numbered per chain.

matchBinding.description: Owner-only vs agentWallet-confirmed payTo counts for mis-binding risk before on-chain feedback.

walletConfirmedShare.description: Percent with one decimal; null when no matched payTo.

matchedPurchases.description: Purchase attempt rows whose payTo matched

matchedSettled.description: The part of matchedPurchases with status settled.

matches.description: Up to 200 across the chains, largest purchases first. chainId names the chain of agentId.

reason.description: Present only when status is unavailable.

scannedAgents.description: Agent rows in the Base owner index.

l1.description:
L1 real-purchase totals. `settled` is a transfer vet402 re-read
on-chain. `delivered` is a settled attempt whose paid request also
answered HTTP 2xx other than 202 Accepted, with a non-empty body. The settlement asset is USDC on Base, Arc, Celo, Solana, Stellar, Arbitrum One and Avalanche C-Chain, USDC.e on Tempo, RLUSD from its fixed issuer on XRPL, and USD1 on BNB Chain. Stellar is re-read for payer, payee, amount and asset, and is published as amount and payee.

`settled` is published at two evidence strengths, and
`settledNonceBound + settledAmountPayeeOnly` always equals
`settled`. The split labels strength. It does not change the
count. Rows that settled before the nonce binding shipped
(2026-09-04T12:00:00Z), and Stellar rows, are not demoted. vet402 does not refute a
seller on evidence it does not hold.

answerCheck.description: Settled purchases in the last `windowDays` whose paid answer was checked offline from data already on the purchase row (`raw_response_meta.answerCheck`). No new purchases. Since 2026-11-17. `shapeSame` / `shapeChanged` count undeclared listings compared to the earliest complete 2xx JSON on that endpoint (not L2 match). Since 2026-11-18.

checkedShare.description: checked divided by settled in the window; null if settled is 0.

shapeChanged.description: Undeclared rows whose shape differs from that baseline (outcome stays unknown; not counted as mismatch).

shapeSame.description: Undeclared rows whose JSON top-level shape matches the endpoint's first complete paid answer (`answerCheck.shapeBaseline` = same).

awaitingReread.description: Attempts at `settle_claimed`: the seller asserted a settlement and vet402 has not yet re-read it on-chain (the daily re-read runs at 14:00 UTC). Counted in attempts, in neither delivered nor inconclusive. Since 2026-09-29.

awaitingRereadOlderThan1d.description: The part of awaitingReread whose attempt is more than 1 day old. Since 2026-09-29.

awaitingRereadOlderThan7d.description: The part of awaitingReread whose attempt is more than 7 days old. A row stays at settle_claimed while the chain read cannot settle it either way, so some rows wait far longer than a day. Since 2026-09-29.

awaitingRereadOldestAttemptAt.description: The oldest attempt still awaiting the re-read (ISO 8601 UTC). Since 2026-09-29.

byChain.description: Per-chain L1 breakdown. Unlike the top-level (L0) byChain this is not mainnet-filtered, so its columns sum to the l1 totals.

chain.description: Join key. Unchanged. BSC stays BSC. stellar:pubnet stays stellar:pubnet. Arbitrum stays Arbitrum. Callers that join on this field keep working.

inconclusive.description: The chain's share of l1.inconclusive — paid attempts held rather than counted against the seller. Not a subset of that chain's settled.

inconclusiveSettled.description: The chain's settled purchases that are held as inconclusive (for example a 4xx after payment). A subset of that chain's settled, so settled minus this is the denominator of the chain's delivery rate.

label.description: Public name of this chain. Base, Solana, Tempo, XRPL, Celo, Arc, Stellar, BNB Chain, Arbitrum One, or Avalanche C-Chain when the chain is one of those. Other chains keep the name in chain. Screens show this field.

network.description: Canonical CAIP-2 id for this chain. eip155:56 when chain is BSC. stellar:pubnet when chain is stellar:pubnet. eip155:42161 when chain is Arbitrum.

byFacilitator.description: L1 purchase rows grouped by facilitator id from row evidence (l1-facilitator.ts): circle_gateway (Circle Gateway batch), xrpl_t54 (xrpl:0), tempo_mpp (eip155:4217), stellar_facilitator (stellar:pubnet). Solana and other rows where the seller-side facilitator cannot be read from published ledger columns are unknown. The unknown bucket is always present.

endpointsSettled.description:
Endpoints, active or not, with at least one settled
row. Equals `endpointsSettledSellerReceipt` +
`endpointsSettledIndexOnly`.

endpointsSettledIndexOnly.description:
Endpoints whose settled rows all carry a transaction
found by vet402's own settlements index
(`settlement_source=vet402_index`), or named in a
Circle Gateway batch
(`settlement_source=circle_gateway`): no seller
receipt. Since 2026-09-29.

endpointsSettledSellerReceipt.description:
Endpoints with at least one settled row whose
transaction the seller named in its settlement
receipt (`settlement_source=seller_claim`). Since
2026-09-29.

inconclusive.description: Paid attempts held rather than counted against the seller (split in inconclusiveByReason). Not a subset of settled since 2026-09-17.

inconclusiveByReason.description: Sums to inconclusive. settled4xx — settled and answered 4xx; unsettled4xx — answered a 4xx other than 402 with no settlement receipt; payerUnfunded — answered 402 or 5xx while vet402's own Base payer wallet was out of USDC (2026-09-13T00:00Z–2026-09-15T23:49Z).

inconclusiveSettled.description: The settled part of inconclusive; settled − delivered − inconclusiveSettled is money that moved without a 4xx and did not count as delivered (a 5xx, a 3xx, a 202, an empty body or no recorded answer).

lastAttemptAt.description: When vet402 last attempted an L1 purchase against any endpoint (ISO 8601 UTC; null before the first attempt). Not filtered by status — an attempt that ended before the signature still says when we last looked. Read it with `spendingHalted`: while the spend is halted these counts do not move, and a quiet day and a halted day are otherwise indistinguishable.

settledAmountPayeeOnly.description: Settled rows where the re-read matched payer, payee, amount and asset and did not bind a one-time value. That tier holds rows that settled before 2026-09-04T12:00:00Z, and it holds Stellar rows. A transfer of the same amount to the same payee can match.

settledCircleGateway.description: Settled rows in a Circle Gateway batch, with no separate transfer to the payee (`settlement_source=circle_gateway`). Since 2026-11-02.

settledLateLinked.description: Settled rows whose transaction the seller did not name: the paid response carried no settlement receipt, and vet402's own settlements index found the transfer afterwards (payer, payee, exact amount, time window) before the same on-chain re-read. A different axis from the two evidence strengths — not part of their sum. The ledger export marks these rows `settlement_source=vet402_index`. Since 2026-09-20.

settledNonceBound.description: Settled rows where the re-read matched the one-time value stored for that purchase (the EIP-3009 authorization nonce on Base, Arc, Celo, BNB Chain, Arbitrum One and Avalanche C-Chain, a memo vet402 wrote on Solana, the indexed memo of a TIP-20 TransferWithMemo on Tempo, the hash of the signed blob on XRPL), so the transaction is the one for that purchase. Stellar is not in this count. The Stellar re-read checks payer, payee, amount and asset.

settledNotDelivered.description: settled − delivered − inconclusiveSettled, published directly (never below 0). Money moved without a 4xx and the paid request did not count as delivered.

settledTimeWindowOk.description: Settled rows whose settlement block time falls within -5/+15 minutes of the attempt. An independent check that survives the missing nonce; a row outside the window is still settled, not refuted.

settledTimeWindowUnknown.description: Settled rows with no settlement block time on record — neither inside nor outside the window.

l1Rates.description: l1.delivered over three denominators, side by side (one decimal, null when the denominator is 0). deliveredOfAttemptsPct divides by l1.attempts, which includes held attempts (l1.inconclusive) and attempts awaiting re-read (l1.awaitingReread); deliveredOfNotHeldPct divides by attempts − inconclusive; deliveredOfFinalOutcomePct divides by attempts − inconclusive − awaitingReread. The denominators are in `denominators`. Since 2026-09-29.

rate_formula.description: Simple ratio formula for l1.delivered shares (pct1, one decimal, null when denominator is 0). Version ratio-pct1-v1.

latestSnapshot.description: Latest snapshot of the PRIMARY catalog (source cdp_bazaar) only. vet402 reads more than one discovery catalog, each with its own snapshot date and its own fetch health, so a second catalog's incomplete fetch must not be read as a caveat on these figures. Every catalog's latest snapshot is in catalogSnapshots.

complete.description: Whether the fetch counts as complete. fetchedCount can be below totalCount on a complete fetch. Null with no record.

cursorPassCompleted.description: cdp_bazaar only: whether the cursor read has closed a full pass.

totalCount.description: The total the catalog reported at that fetch. It is not the count of active listings.

operatorEndpointsExcluded.description: How many catalog endpoints were left out of every count in this response because they pay an address vet402 controls — a measurer is not a neutral third party in its own numbers. The same exclusion is applied to totalEndpoints, byChain, coverage7d and the daily rollup behind /api/v1/observatory/history (as of 2026-09-19; each rollup run restates the trailing recomputeWindowDays days, so the step sits at the oldest day still inside that window at the first run after 2026-09-19, and that boundary then stays where it is — a restated day is not restated back; an older day restated because its raw L1 totals changed carries the population in force at that restatement). This count does not distinguish "the denylist matched nothing" from "the denylist is empty" — operatorExclusionConfigured does.

operatorExclusionConfigured.description: Whether that exclusion list is configured at all. false means the rule is a no-op on this response, whatever operatorEndpointsExcluded says; true with operatorEndpointsExcluded 0 means the rule is on and nothing matched. The addresses themselves are not published.

publicApiUsage.description: Call counts per UTC day from client_usage_daily, for calls made without an API key. Rows from vet402's own monitors and observatory clients are left out. decision counts GET /api/v1/resources/{id}/decision. check counts GET /api/v1/check, a separate entry point, so it is not part of decision. sdk counts every route called by a client that names itself vet402-sdk/<semver>, and those calls are not counted again under decision or check. mcp counts rows whose client is vet402-mcp/<semver>. mcp:* routes from any other client are counted in otherRoutes. Current SDK and MCP releases may not send that User-Agent and then appear as other. These counts are not added to l1.attempts.

otherRoutes.description: Other clients, including mcp:* routes from unnamed clients.

weeklyExternal.description: Calls without an API key per UTC week starting Monday, every route, leaving out vet402's own monitors and observatory clients, vet402's own site, crawlers, and MCP connection handshakes that call no tool (mcp:initialize).

publishedFail.description: Endpoints whose newest probes publish as fail and whose catalog status is not delisted. A delisted fail streak is withdrawnFail. Since 2026-10-24.

publishedFailProbeOlderThan30d.description: The part of `publishedFail` whose latest failing probe is more than 30 days old. Same fail definition as `publishedFail`; only the age window is split out. Since 2026-11-20.

publishedPass.description:
Endpoints on record whose latest L0 probe passed,
including delisted endpoints — it can exceed
`activeEndpoints`.

publishedPassActive.description:
The part of `publishedPass` on active records.
Since 2026-09-29.

publishedPassActiveProbeOlderThan7d.description:
The part of `publishedPassActive` whose latest probe is
more than 7 days old (a pass stands until the next
probe). Since 2026-09-29.

spendingHalted.description: Whether vet402 has halted its own L1 spending. This is a fact about the measurer, not about any seller or about x402. While it is true the l1 counts do not move, so read `l1.lastAttemptAt` alongside it before quoting the figures as current. It is read on every request rather than from the aggregate cache, and it reads true when the flag itself could not be read (a money gate fails closed).

withdrawnFail.description: Endpoints with catalog status delisted whose newest probes would publish as fail. Left out of publishedFail. A pass on a delisted endpoint stays in publishedPass. Since 2026-10-24.

get.description:
Authenticated. Returns the exact message this API key must have signed
by the receiving wallet, plus the catalog endpoints currently paying
that wallet. The signature binds wallet AND this key, so a signature
for another key cannot route someone else's `endpoint.delisted` events.

**Message form changed 2026-09-05 (S-6).** Every signed message now
opens with `vet402.com — <purpose>` and carries a `domain: vet402.com`
line, so the wallet's signing view shows which site is asking; the
`issued` line states its own `(valid 10 minutes)`; and the last line
says what the signature does and that it moves no funds. Signatures
over the pre-2026-09-05 form are still accepted until
**2026-09-21T00:00:00Z** (the response carries `legacy_message: true`);
after that they are refused with `signature_message_legacy_expired`
rather than a bare `signature_mismatch`. Always fetch the current
message from the GET preview instead of building it locally.

get.description:
Returns the exact message a payee wallet must sign to register via
`POST /api/v1/payees/verify`, plus the `issued` timestamp embedded in
it (echo the same value back in the POST — the signature only verifies
against the exact message it signed). No API key; throttled to 30
requests per minute per IP like the other key-less paths. The message
binds wallet + name, optionally a `url` line (so a published proof
cannot overwrite the profile link), and an `issued` line (so an old
signature cannot be replayed to roll back a newer edit). `issued` must
be within 10 minutes of the server clock at POST time.

**Message form changed 2026-09-05 (S-6).** Every signed message now
opens with `vet402.com — <purpose>` and carries a `domain: vet402.com`
line, so the wallet's signing view shows which site is asking; the
`issued` line states its own `(valid 10 minutes)`; and the last line
says what the signature does and that it moves no funds. Signatures
over the pre-2026-09-05 form are still accepted until
**2026-09-21T00:00:00Z** (the response carries `legacy_message: true`);
after that they are refused with `signature_message_legacy_expired`
rather than a bare `signature_mismatch`. Always fetch the current
message from the GET preview instead of building it locally.

parameters.description: Optional https profile URL; when set it is bound into the signed message.

issued.description: Echo this exact value back in the POST body.

post.description:
Free, no API key. Sign the message from `GET /api/v1/payees/verify` (or
build it yourself per that endpoint's description) with the payee
wallet — a valid EIP-191 signature is the proof of control and the
main anti-abuse gate, backed by an 8-per-minute-per-IP write throttle
(EOA wallets only). Publishes a public profile at `/payee/{wallet}`
and an embeddable SVG badge at `/api/badge/{wallet}.svg`. Verification
proves wallet control only; trust scores stay computed independently.

`url` and `issued` are part of the signed bytes. Writes are monotonic
on `issued`: replaying an older still-valid signature returns `409
stale_signature` instead of rolling back a newer (name, url) edit.

issued.description: The exact `issued` value from GET (or self-generated, within 10 minutes of now).

400.description:
Bad request — includes `invalid_wallet_address`, `url_must_be_https`,
`invalid_issued_at`, `signature_expired` (issued outside the
10-minute window), and `signature_mismatch` (whose response body
also carries `expectedMessage`, so a rejected signature is
self-diagnosing).

409.description:
`stale_signature` — the signed `issued` is not newer than the
currently stored one, so the write was rejected (replay guard).

503.description: Store unavailable (schema not yet migrated, or DB unreachable).

get.description:
Deprecated since 2026-09-02: use
`GET /api/v1/resources/{resourceId}/decision?role=payer` for the
endpoint you are about to pay (`GET /api/v1/resolve?q={url}` finds its
`resourceId`). This score rates the wallet as a whole, not that
endpoint, and can say ALLOW where the decision says WARN or BLOCK.
Its value is unchanged; since 2026-09-29 the response says so itself
(`deprecated`, `deprecation`, and the `Deprecation` / `Link` headers).

Buyer-side counterpart to `/api/v1/agents/{agentId}/score` and
`/api/v1/wallets/{address}/score`,
which screen the caller of an x402 route. This endpoint screens the *recipient*:
"should my agent pay this wallet?" before an x402 payment is sent.

Combines the wallet's own settlement receiving history (payments attested via
`POST /api/v1/payments/x402` where it was the payee), wallet-age/tx-count health, an
exit-scam-shaped outflow check (received funds then drained them), and any prior
`verdict_outcomes` labels naming this wallet.

Never 404s for an unfamiliar wallet — a wallet with little or no receiving
history still returns `200` with `dataDepth: "thin"`, so integrators can decide
how much to trust a thin-data score rather than being blocked outright.

post.description:
Keyless read of one payment receipt. No wallet. The body is
paymentResponse (the seller PAYMENT-RESPONSE header, base64 JSON)
or network plus transaction. vet402 reads the transaction on Base,
Celo, Arbitrum One, Avalanche C-Chain, BNB Chain, Solana, Arc,
Tempo, XRPL and Stellar, the chains it reads again after a purchase.
The answer carries found, network, tx, block, from, to, asset,
amount in atomic units, status, explorer and as_of. status is
confirmed, failed, not_found or unsupported_network. A chain outside
that set comes back as unsupported_network. 20 requests a minute
per IP. The chain read stops at 8 seconds. This route does not pay
and does not sign.

post.description:
Call after x402 payment verification. Idempotent on `txHash`.
Settlement history is weighted into trust scores (SCORE_WEIGHTS.x402).

`signature` is optional but load-bearing: without a valid EIP-191
signature by `wallet` over the canonical attestation message, the row
is still recorded but `ownershipVerified` is false and it never counts
toward any score. Since 2026-09-05 that message names the site and
states what the signature causes:

```
vet402.com — x402 settlement attestation
domain: vet402.com
wallet: {wallet, lowercase}
tx: {txHash, lowercase}
Effect: this settlement will be counted toward the public score of the wallet above on vet402.com.
This signature moves no funds.
```

A signature over the pre-2026-09-05 form still proves ownership until
**2026-09-21T00:00:00Z** and the response then carries
`legacyMessage: true`; after that date it proves nothing (the row is
recorded unscored) and the response carries `legacyMessageExpired`.

amount.description: Payment amount as decimal string (smallest unit OK)

signature.description:
EIP-191 signature by `wallet` over the canonical
attestation message (see above). Omitting it records the
settlement with `ownershipVerified: false`.

Rebuilds the verdict receipt message and checks the EIP-191 signature
with verifyMessage. No API key. A match returns ok true. A changed
field returns ok false and error invalid_signature. A field vet402
cannot read returns 400 invalid_input. 30 requests per minute per IP.
The message and the canonical input are in the verdict receipt section
of the docs. When VET402_RECEIPT_SIGNER_KEY is unset, GET /api/v1/check
and GET /api/v1/resources/{resourceId}/decision omit receipt and the
rest of the body stays as it is.

Summary of a frozen UTC month of purchase rows. The content hash is SHA-256
over the frozen CSV body (data rows only, no header): same columns as the
default export. Rows in the hash are sorted by attempted_at as a
second-precision ISO-8601 string, then purchase_id (the live export sorts by
full attempted_at first, so sub-second ties can differ). GET /api/v1/reports/{month}.csv
returns that body. Before
vet402 stores a freeze, the response is 404 with not_frozen_yet. An open month
answers 400 with month_not_closed. Key-less. 120 requests per minute. Since 2026-11-27.

get.description:
When VET402_RECEIPT_SIGNER_KEY is set, the body also carries receipt.
POST /api/v1/receipts/verify checks that signature with no API key.
When the variable is unset, receipt is omitted and the rest of the body stays as it is.
Product spec §8.3 / §9.1. `role=payer` (default) answers "what did"
vet402 record when it paid this URL in the last 30 days?" from L0
liveness, L1 settle-through and L2 conformance. An ALLOW can carry
`l2_undeclared`: the listing declared no output to compare with.
`role=payee` answers "should this
seller serve this payer?" and requires `payer`. The response carries
`facts` and `recommendation` together. The transitional 0–100 `score`
is left out unless `include_score=1` (since 2026-09-29.3); when
returned it carries `superseded_by: "recommendation"` and is not the
basis of the recommendation. Every reason code is listed in
`DecisionReasonCode` and in the table at /docs/api#reason-codes.
`caller_dialect` (v1|v2) lets the engine WARN on a wall that speaks a
different x402 dialect than your client. `allow_without_l1=true` is
the operator's explicit opt-in to ALLOW a resource vet402 has not yet
purchased from, or whose last delivery is older than 30 days. Send `Idempotency-Key` to retry without spending a
second rate-limit unit. 1 unit per call.
Key-less reads (AQ-053, 2026-09-07): with no `Authorization` header
the same body is returned under a per-IP window of 60/min
(since 2026-11-15, 10/min before). Without a key the transitional
`score` is not read, so `include_score=1` returns `score: null`
(since 2026-11-15). The recommendation does not use it.
(`rate_limited` on 429, `RateLimit-*` headers on the wire);
`Idempotency-Key` and customer allow/block lists apply only to keyed
calls. A present-but-invalid key is still 401, never anonymous.
`DECISION_KEYLESS_READ=0` restores key-only access.
Caller policy (2026-09-07, role=payer only): send `amount_usd` (what the
402 asks), `max_per_tx_usd` (your ceiling, default 1) and/or
`min_l1_deliveries` (floor on vet402's delivered L1 purchases) and/or
`require_vet402_allow` (default `true`, the SDK's `requireVet402Allow`)
and the same document gains `caller_policy` — the caller's own rule
applied server-side, in the SDK's words (`price_above_ceiling`,
`evidence_unavailable`, `payee_recommendation_block`,
`payee_recommendation_not_allow`, `insufficient_delivery_evidence`).
With `require_vet402_allow=true` a WARN refuses with
`payee_recommendation_not_allow`, exactly as the SDK's default does;
`false` waives the WARN and needs `min_l1_deliveries` ≥ 1 or the call
is 400 `invalid_policy` (waive the verdict, put a floor in its place).
It sits beside `recommendation` and never rewrites it; BLOCK and
degraded are never lifted by a floor or a waiver; without these queries
the body is byte-identical to before. A bad value is 400 with the SDK's
own word (`invalid_amount_usd`, `invalid_policy`,
`invalid_evidence_policy`); a policy query with role=payee is 400
`invalid_policy`. An unknown resource stays 404 (the SDK judges those
from the 402's payTo and the payee score).

parameters.description: Since 2026-09-29.3. `1` adds the transitional payee `score` (marked `deprecated` and `superseded_by: "recommendation"`, not used for the decision). Without it the key is absent. Any other value is 400 `invalid_include_score`.
parameters.name: include_score

parameters.description: What the 402 asks, in USD. Compared with `max_per_tx_usd` (role=payer only). Any of the three policy queries adds `caller_policy` to the response.
parameters.name: amount_usd

parameters.description: The caller's per-payment ceiling in USD. Default equals the SDK's DEFAULT_MAX_PER_TX_USD.
parameters.name: max_per_tx_usd

parameters.description: Floor on `facts.l1.n_delivered` (vet402's own L1 purchases delivered in the last 30 days). The subgraph floor is not evaluated here — see `caller_policy.not_evaluated`.
parameters.name: min_l1_deliveries

parameters.description: Mirror of the SDK's `policy.requireVet402Allow`. `true` (default) refuses any recommendation other than ALLOW with `payee_recommendation_not_allow`; `false` waives a WARN and requires `min_l1_deliveries` ≥ 1 (400 `invalid_policy` otherwise). Only the literal strings `true` / `false` are accepted.
parameters.name: require_vet402_allow

query order hashed as sha256("<METHOD> <url>") — which answers for
the listed URL. `error` stays `not_found`. `host_known` is `true` when
`url` was given and vet402 has listings on its host (the id may be
another spelling of a listed URL: resolve the URL with
`/api/v1/resolve?q=<url>&method=<METHOD>` before paying, and do not
treat the seller as unlisted), `false` when it has none, and `null`
when `url` was not given or is not an https URL.

get.description:
docs/rwa/SPEC.md §7 and patches 018 to 023 (rwa-recon-0.3). Rebuilds the
address's history in the canonical Stock Tokens of Robinhood's own
list (195, frozen in packages/rwa/registry.json): token Transfers,
Uniswap v3/v4 swaps verified against the official factory and
PoolManager, and the Chainlink feed for the tokens that have one (33).
Scope, stated in `scope`: with an Alchemy endpoint (patch 020, live in
production since 2026-09-30), every canonical token that ever moved to
or from the address, including positions it sold out of. Without one,
tokens held at `as_of`, NVDA, and canonical tokens those tokens'
transactions moved. A position opened and closed in another token is
then not scanned, and `gaps` says so (`exited_positions_not_scanned`).
`lookalikes` (patch 021) lists tokens the wallet met that copy a Stock
Token or USDG. They are never counted: not in `tokens`, not in any USD
figure, not in `evidence`. `lookalikes_scope` says how far that search
went. Each token carries `corporate_actions` (patch 022): every
UIMultiplierUpdated of the token since genesis, with the wallet's
shares before and after. The response header `X-Facts-Hash` is the
anchor hash of this body (patch 023, hash material v2 from
rwa-recon-0.3), so a reader can compare it with an Anchored event.
Every movement is classified as `transfer`, `univ3`, `univ4` or
`other_unparsed`; nothing is dropped. Realized PnL is FIFO per token;
a Stock-for-Stock trade is not priced. `usd` is null with `usd_reason`
`feed_stale` (26h+ or oracle paused) or `no_feed`. Each token's
`replayed_raw` must equal its `raw`; when it does not, `gaps` carries
`balance_mismatch` and `r1_status: unverified`. There is no opinion field
on this path. Key-less; 10/min/IP (counted in the shared store, so it
holds across instances). One address is cached for 5 minutes and one
reconstruction runs at a time, both per server instance. The route
answers within 20 seconds (patch 020). A read still running then keeps
going, the answer is 503 `still_reading` with Retry-After, and the retry
joins that read.

lookalikes.description: SPEC patch 021. Tokens that copy a Stock Token or USDG, met in the wallet's transfers. Never counted.

imitates.description: the canonical ticker or USDG it copies

needs_review.description: Stock Token proxy code outside Robinhood's list

complete.description: true only when every ERC-20 transfer to and from the wallet up to as_of_block was read

realized_usd.description: Sum over tokens of FIFO realized; null when no sale could be priced against a known cost

history_not_walked.description: tokens seen only inside walked transactions (gap history_not_walked)

scanned.description: tokens whose own transfer history was walked

corporate_actions.description:
SPEC patch 022. Every UIMultiplierUpdated of this token from genesis to
`as_of_block`, oldest first. Absent when the read failed (gap
`corporate_actions_not_read`). Realized PnL is on raw amounts, so it does not move.

held.description: the wallet held the token right after the update; null when its history was not walked

replayed_raw.description: What replaying this token's classified events leaves the address holding

usd.description: null while the feed is stale or when the token has no feed

unrealized_usd.description: USD mark of everything held; null unless every held token has a fresh feed

X-Facts-Hash.description: Anchor hash of the body (SPEC patch 023). Hash material v2 for rwa-recon-0.3 and later.

400.description: `invalid_address` — not 20-byte hex, or chain other than 4663

sent_tx_count.description: transactions the address has sent (its nonce)

404.description:
`no_stock_token_activity`: the address holds none of the canonical
Stock Tokens and no history in scope was found (SPEC patch 020).
The body states what was checked. `Cache-Control: public,
max-age=60, s-maxage=300, stale-while-revalidate=60` (patch 024):
the CDN keeps it 5 minutes and serves it stale for 60 s at most.
`history_checked` is `every_canonical_token` when the transfers of
every canonical token were read, or `nvda_only` when only today's
balances and NVDA's incoming transfers were (gap
`exited_positions_not_scanned`).

422.description:
`wallet_too_large` (SPEC patch 020): the wallet needs more than one
request can do (more than 6 tokens to walk on the public RPC, more
than 600 transactions to replay on either path, or with Alchemy more
than 30 tokens held or moved or more than 20,000 Stock Token
transfers). A read stops as soon as it passes a limit, so `found`
is then the count it stopped at and `detail` says "more than". With
Alchemy, more than 30 tokens held is answered before any transfer
read, and `found` is the count held (SPEC patch 026). The body lists
`held` (symbols), `held_tokens`, `limit` and `detail`. Vercel's CDN
does not keep a 422. This server keeps it 5 minutes per instance.
Not rebuilt.

503.description:
SPEC patch 020. Always with Retry-After and a body
`{ error, retry_after_sec, detail }`. `too_busy`: another wallet is
being rebuilt on this instance. `still_reading`: the read took
longer than this request waits (20 s). It keeps running and the
retry joins it. `chain_unavailable`: the chain RPC failed.

get.description:
docs/rwa/SPEC.md patch 017. Returns exactly what getRwaFacts returns,
at 60 requests/min/IP instead of 10. The free route is unchanged.
Paying does not jump the queue: one reconstruction at a time per
instance is shared with the free route and the /rwa page.
Without a `PAYMENT-SIGNATURE` header the answer is 402 with
`PAYMENT-REQUIRED` (base64 JSON, also the body): scheme `exact`,
network `eip155:4663`, asset USDG
`0x5fc5360D0400a0Fd4f2af552ADD042D716F1d168`, amount `10000`
(0.01 USDG), `assetTransferMethod: permit2`, payTo
`0x973cD8a91A771C2C04C6036888F8175D6b4F6227`, facilitator Dexter.
With the header: the terms and the Permit2 signature are checked
locally, the payment is verified at the facilitator, the record is
built, and only then settled. 404, 422 and 503 carry `charged: false`.
Once settle has been sent the record is returned, unless the
facilitator answered `success: false` (402, no money moved).
`X-Payment-Status: settled` comes with `PAYMENT-RESPONSE` (base64 JSON
with the tx hash); `X-Payment-Status: unknown` means the facilitator
did not give a clear answer and the payment may or may not have moved.

get.description:
The data behind the counts on `/sellers` (since 2026-09-29): one row
per active Base listing (records opened for a seller's re-test request
included), classified by its latest purchase row with
the same function the page uses. Counting rows by `outcome` gives the
page's totals. The page is not indexed while its attribution is under
review, and this file is served with `X-Robots-Tag: noindex` for the
same reason.

Columns: `host`, `endpoint_id`, `resource_key`, `outcome`
(`delivered` | `pending` — a receipt awaiting the on-chain re-read, or
a signed attempt whose result is not known yet | `seller` — seller's
side | `vet402` — vet402's side, including limits hit before signing |
`unsorted` — not sorted yet | `not_bought` — tried, vet402 did not
sign | `not_tried` — no purchase row on a Base network; a listing
bought only on another chain reads not_tried here, so read /decision
for it), `fix_mode` (the failure kind;
blank for delivered, pending and not_tried), `side_label` (the words
of the page's "whose side" column), `confirmed_seller` (`true` when a
seller's-side failure was seen on 2 or more UTC days; blank unless
`outcome=seller`), `held_reason` (as in the ledger export),
`latest_attempted_at`, `latest_status`, `latest_network`,
`latest_http_status_paid`, `purchase_id` (the latest row's id — the
`purchase_id` column of `/api/v1/observatory/export.csv` and the
`subject_id` in `/api/v1/observatory/corrections`),
`in_ledger_export` (whether that row appears in the ledger export;
rows in vet402-side states such as `halted` or `request_error` do
not), `attribution_review` (`under_review` on `outcome=seller` rows,
blank otherwise, since 2026-10-21). Which side a failed purchase is on
is still under review, and the `x-vet402-column-notes` header starts
with that sentence. The definitions also travel in the `x-vet402-column-notes`
header; the retrieval time in `x-vet402-retrieved-at`. IP-throttled to
6/min; CDN-cached for up to 15 minutes. Takes no query parameters: any
is 400 `invalid_query` (since 2026-09-29). Reads the store one export
at a time across all callers (503 `export_busy` with `Retry-After`).

Counts of decision API answers made with a key, for one published chain
and one closed UTC month. Figures come from keyed decision rows. The first
read after 00:00 UTC on the 3rd day of the next month stores the figures,
and later reads return that stored copy. Answers are summed by relation.
A labeled relation shows the number of owners. Fewer than 3 owners shows
<3 and leaves the call count out. An unclassified relation leaves the call
count out. This response lists keyed decision answers. Since 2026-11-26,
key-less calls with a known network are counted in client_usage_daily_network by UTC day,
client, route and network. Those counts are not in this response.
The response leaves out the key, the email address, and the name.
Key-less. 60 requests per minute.
`chain` must be a published network id. `eip155:42220` is published.
A slug that names that same network, such as `celo`, is accepted.
An `eip155:` prefix is read in lower case, so `EIP155:42220` is `eip155:42220`.
`month` is `YYYY-MM` in UTC, from 2026 through 2100.
